newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel may raise reserve requirement.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel may raise reserve requirement.

text.p: The Bank of Israel may raise the reserve requirements for commercial banks in an effort to combat growing liquidity in the economy, financial sources said on Tuesday.
The Bank of Israel would not comment on the reports.

One source, confirming a report in the daily newspaper Haaretz this morning, said the central bank was considering raising the reserve requirement by five percentage points. That would raise the requirement to between eight and 11 percent, depending on the term of the deposit.
The central bank pays no interest on the reserve requirement, so that the commercial banks would likely lower their deposit rates if the measure were implemented.
The source said the bank had been holding discussions on the matter but it was unclear when a decision would be made. "The proposal had been circulating for some time," the source said.
Haaretz said Governor Jacob Frenkel would present a proposal to the Bank of Israel advisory committee on Wednesday.

Hezi Gutman, head of the economics department at First International Bank of Israel, said a decision to raise the reserve requirement would mark a retreat for the Bank of Israel's long-term policy of reducing intervention in the money market.

However, the bank faces increasing pressure to absorb excess liquidity in the economy. The government was running big budget deficits at the end of last year, reaching 4.4 billion shekels in December alone. The deficit is being increasingly financed by foreign borrowing.
The bank's other monetary tools, principally the Makam debt certificates, have been fully exploited.
